title: Provision of Staking Services for Virtual Assets from Custodial Services
summary: On 7 April 2025, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) issued a circular addressed to all Authorized Institutions, titled 'Provision of Staking Services for Virtual Assets from Custodial Services.' Staking involves committing virtual assets to a proof-of-stake blockchain's validation process, typically in exchange for rewards; this circular addresses that activity specifically where an Authorized Institution provides it in connection with virtual assets the institution already holds for clients through its own custodial arrangements. HKMA filed the circular under its Banking Conduct & Enforcement (Consumer Protection) and Fintech (Virtual Assets) categories, and the circular cross-references HKMA's earlier circular of 20 February 2024 on the provision of custodial services for digital assets, positioning the new guidance as an extension of that existing custody framework rather than a standalone regime for staking.
why_it_matters: Staking is a common way for holders of proof-of-stake virtual assets to earn rewards, but doing it through a bank raises custody-style risks for the client if something goes wrong. This circular is how HKMA, Hong Kong's banking regulator, addresses that specific activity for the Authorized Institutions it supervises, building on its existing digital-asset custody rules rather than creating a wholly separate regime.
